record.what_it_does: CRM platform for sales, marketing and service with a broad public API.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 for multi-account apps. Static-auth (private) tokens and service keys are single-account Bearer tokens. A developer API key (hapikey) is used only for a few developer features. Client-credentials tokens are used only for the webhooks journal.
record.access_notes: A free developer account and free developer test accounts (90-day enterprise trial) are enough to build and test. OAuth apps distributed to multiple accounts need OAuth with distribution set to marketplace. The auth page I fetched mentions no app review step, but HubSpot's marketplace listing process may include one. Private distribution is limited to 10 accounts.
record.api_breadth_notes: CRM objects (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, custom objects), associations, search, engagements, pipelines, properties, plus marketing, CMS, conversations and more. I did not count the operations.
record.mcp_notes: mcp.hubspot.com. It uses OAuth 2.0 with a user-level app and gives read and write access to CRM data.
record.blocker_notes: Self-serve OAuth is available. Check whether the marketplace listing for public distribution needs app review.

evidence.quote: Service keys provide a way to query HubSpot's REST APIs directly
limit distribution of your app to a single authorized account
enables you to give any MCP-compatible AI tool or agent secure read and write access to your HubSpot CRM data.
All API endpoints require OAuth 2.0 authentication.
Developer test accounts are free HubSpot accounts with access to a 90-day trial of many enterprise features.

record.needs_human: Confirm whether the app marketplace listing needs review before arbitrary customers can install a public OAuth app. Confirm the published OpenAPI spec (I believe it is in HubSpot's public API spec repo, but I did not open it). The webhooks page I fetched covered only the v4 journal API. It did not describe the classic v3 webhooks, which push to a target URL.
